title: Two pointers: same direction
learn: read/write pointers for in-place filtering, subsequence matching, merging
hook: "Do it in place with O(1) extra memory" is one of the most common interview follow-ups. A slow write pointer and a fast read pointer is usually the answer: Remove Duplicates, Move Zeroes, Sort Colors.

explain.prompt: Explain how you'd remove duplicates from a sorted array in place, and why it's O(n) time and O(1) space.
keyPoints: a fast pointer reads every element, a slow pointer marks where the next kept element goes
sorted input: an element is new when it differs from the last kept value
write it at the slow pointer and advance; everything before the slow pointer is the answer
one pass, O(n) time, O(1) extra space, no deletions (which would be O(n) each)
